_comment: Real-world requests. 'skills' are the optional skills a user would tick. 'checks' are scored automatically on the design the model returns.

cases.request: A round pen holder for my desk, about 80 mm across and 100 mm tall, with a solid bottom.
A small box with a snap-on lid to keep 10 SD cards standing up in a row. SD cards are 32 x 24 x 2.1 mm.
A clip I can screw to the underside of my desk to hold one 6 mm cable. Use one countersunk screw.
An L-shaped shelf bracket for an 18 mm shelf board, 150 mm deep shelf, two screws into the wall and one into the shelf.
A case for a Raspberry Pi 4 with an opening for the USB and Ethernet ports on one end and vents in the lid.
A drawer organiser tray, inside 200 x 120 x 40 mm, divided into 3 equal compartments along its length.
A 400 mm long, 100 mm wide desk tray, 30 mm deep. My printer bed is 220 x 220 mm so it must come in pieces that slot together.
A 300 mm tall vase with a bulging middle. My printer is only 250 mm tall, so split it and pin the pieces together.
A box for tea bags, 150 x 80 x 70 mm outside, cut horizontally near the top so the top part comes off and is held on with 6 x 3 mm magnets.
A desk phone stand that holds a phone in landscape at about 60 degrees, for phones up to 12 mm thick with a case.
A sturdy wall hook for a backpack, mounted with two screws.
A holder for 8 AA batteries standing upright in a 2 x 4 grid.
A filament spool axle: a tube that fits through a 52 mm spool hole, 70 mm long, with a flange at one end.
A grippy knob with a captive M6 nut so I can make a hand-tightened bolt.
A plant pot 120 mm across and 110 mm tall with drainage holes, and a separate saucer it sits in.
An under-desk headphone hanger, screwed to the desk underside, with a 25 mm wide curved support for the headband.
A tray for small screws with a 4 x 3 grid of square compartments, each 25 mm square and 20 mm deep.
A round lamp base 120 mm across and 50 mm tall, with a hole on top for a 10 mm threaded lamp pipe, a cable hole in the side and a screwed-on bottom plate.
A 450 x 150 x 6 mm plain sign plate for my 256 mm printer, in pieces joined with dovetails, with two keyhole-ish screw holes to hang it.
Coasters for my mugs: the photo shows a mug standing next to a credit card, and the mug base is about 1.1 card widths across. Make a coaster with a 3 mm raised rim.
